cards.text: Last time, King Asa of Judah cried out to the LORD, the LORD struck down the Cushite army, and Judah came home to Jerusalem loaded with plunder. BIG win. Now the Spirit of God comes upon a man named Azariah son of Oded.

cards.question: With the Spirit of God on him, where does Azariah go?

cards.text: Azariah tells him, "Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin." Friend, when a man with the Spirit of God on him opens with "Listen to me," you put your phone DOWN.

cards.question: According to Azariah, when is the LORD with Asa and Judah?
Azariah says the LORD will stay with Judah even if they forsake Him.

cards.text: Then Azariah looks back: for many years, Israel has been without the true God, without a priest to instruct them, and without the law. That's a kitchen with no recipe and nobody to teach you, friend, and that's not baking, that's just flour EVERYWHERE.

cards.question: Azariah says that when distress hit, Israel looked to other nations for help instead of turning to the LORD.

cards.text: Azariah says those were rough days. There was no safety for travelers, and nation was crushed by nation, and city by city.

cards.question: Azariah says that back in those rough days, God afflicted them with all kinds of adversity.

cards.text: Then Azariah says, "But as for you, be strong; do not be discouraged, for your work will be rewarded." Friend, the last time I worked that hard, my reward was a one-way trip to the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Azariah said to be strong and not be discouraged. When Asa heard the prophecy, he took ___.
With fresh courage, Asa gets to work in Judah, Benjamin and the cities he captured in Ephraim's hill country. He removes the detestable ___.
With the idols gone, what does Asa restore in front of the portico of the LORD's temple?

cards.text: Next, Asa assembles all Judah and Benjamin. People from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon who had settled among them show up too.

cards.question: Great numbers had come over to Asa from Israel because they saw that the LORD his God was with him.

cards.text: So they all gather in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign. That many people, one city, one date? Friend, I can't get THREE people in a group chat to agree on a time.

cards.question: In Jerusalem, they sacrifice seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep to the LORD. Where did all those animals come from?
After the sacrifices, the people enter into a covenant to ___ the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and soul.
The covenant comes with a hard rule. What would happen to whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel?

answers.text: They would be put to death
They would be sent out of Judah
They would pay a fine to the priests

cards.question: The covenant's hard rule applied only to the men of Judah, not the women.

cards.text: They take an oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, trumpets and rams' horns. Mags would've fit RIGHT in, because that's the only volume she's got.

cards.question: All Judah ___ over the oath, because they had sworn it with all their ___.
Judah sought the LORD earnestly, and He was found by them. What does the LORD give them?

cards.text: Then King Asa deals with someone in his own family: his grandmother Maacah. He removes her from her position as queen mother.

cards.question: King Asa removes his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she plotted to take his throne.

cards.text: Maacah had made a detestable Asherah pole, so Asa chops it down, crushes it, and burns it in the Kidron Valley. Chopped, crushed AND burned, friend, that pole is NOT making a comeback.

cards.question: Asa cleared idols out of Judah, and the high places were removed from Israel as well.
Even with the high places still standing in Israel, how is Asa's heart described?

cards.text: Asa also brings into the house of God the silver, the gold and the articles that he and his father had dedicated.

cards.question: With the house of God stocked and Judah at rest, there was no war until the ___ year of Asa's reign.

cards.text: And that's where we leave King Asa for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story isn't done yet.

findings.problem: Azariah's central promise in 15:2, 'If you seek Him, He will be found by you,' is never told or asked. Card 5 covers only the 'forsake' half. This seek-and-found line is the thread of the whole passage. It returns in 15:4, in the covenant to seek the LORD (15:12) and in its fulfillment (15:15), but the baker never meets the promise itself.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Verse 15:4 appears only as a False statement about looking to other nations. No card ever tells what actually happened: in their distress Israel turned to the LORD, sought Him, and He was found by them. This is the key example behind Azariah's message, and the baker learns only what didn't happen.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'soldiers' and 'walls' don't fit 'the detestable ___'. Removing 'detestable walls' or 'detestable soldiers' reads as silly, so 'idols' stands out as the only sensible choice.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'blame' makes 'a covenant to blame the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and soul' silly. 'Test' is also weak, so 'seek' stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The second blank's answer, 'heart', is given away by the question on card 5 of this stop: 'with all their heart and soul.' 'Heart' wasn't card 5's answer. It sat in that card's question text, which the baker has already read.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Then King Asa deals with someone in his own family' adds an order of events. The text says only 'King Asa also removed his grandmother Maacah' (15:16) and doesn't place it after the oath.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The closing 'story isn't over' story card cites 2 Chronicles 15:19 but tells no verse content. 15:19 was already asked on card 17. The docs say a story card cites the verses it tells, and the JSON needs a verses value, but they don't say what to cite when the card is only the 'story isn't over' line.
findings.question: What should the verses field be on a closing story card that tells no verses: the passage's last verse, the whole passage, or something else?
